_comment: Goldens for the agent-loop suite.
The routing suite asks one question: given a sentence, which tool? This asks
the harder one: put the model in the real loop, with tools that answer back,
and does it finish the job? Multi-turn, so it can look something up and then
act on what it found — and so it can also loop, give up, or do the work
twice, none of which a single-turn eval can see.
Every case runs against STUB tools that record instead of acting. A suite
that created real battles for real classes would be a worse problem than the
one it detects.
expect:
mustCall     tools that have to be asked for, in any order
mustNotCall  tools that must not be — usually the plausible wrong one
args         assertions on the first call to a named tool
once         side-effecting tools the model must not ask for twice
finishes     the loop must end because the model stopped, not because it
hit the iteration cap
maxTurns     an upper bound on model turns; a task done in two turns and a
task done in eleven cost very different amounts
saysNothingOf  strings that must NOT appear in the final message — used to
catch a model that claims work it never did
thresholdNote: Looser than routing, and deliberately. A loop has more ways to be almost-right — an extra lookup, a verbose finish — and holding it to 100% would make the suite noise. Below 80% the agent is not reliably completing work.

cases.name: Set a class battle, end to end
cases.title: Fractions battle for JSS1
cases.description: Set JSS1 a Mathematics battle on fractions — 10 questions, medium difficulty.

cases.name: Look up who is struggling, then act on it
cases.title: Help the weakest learners in JSS1
cases.description: Find out which JSS1 learners are doing worst in Mathematics, then set those learners a battle on the topic they are weakest at.

expect.note: The real multi-turn case: the second tool's arguments can only come from the first tool's answer. A model that assigns before looking up has not done the task, even if a battle exists at the end.

cases.name: Does not do the work twice
cases.title: Self study for JSS1
cases.description: Assign JSS1 self study on the water cycle for Basic Science, due Friday. Confirm it was assigned.

expect.note: The stub returns success in a shape that does not obviously say so, which is what made a task produce twenty battles once. The replay cache should stop a second execution; this checks the model does not keep ASKING either, since every ask is another billed turn.

cases.name: Reports a failure instead of inventing success
cases.title: Battle for JSS4
cases.description: Set JSS4 a Mathematics battle on fractions.

expect.note: JSS4 does not exist, and the tool says so. The failure worth catching is a model that reports the work as done anyway — a teacher who believes it will not find out until the class does not sit the battle.

cases.name: Answers a question without reaching for a tool
cases.title: Question about the platform
cases.description: What is the difference between a class battle and a study review?

expect.note: A question, not an instruction. Tool-happy models assign something to prove they were useful; here the whole job is to answer and stop.

cases.name: One learner means a review, not a battle
cases.title: Check on priya
cases.description: I want to test just priya on fractions in JSS1 Mathematics and see how she did.

expect.note: The distinction the endpoint enforces and a model reliably fudges: a one-learner battle is refused outright, so getting audience wrong here is a task that cannot complete.

cases.name: Picks the right teaching tool and stops
cases.title: Podcast on photosynthesis
cases.description: Make a 5 minute podcast about photosynthesis for JSS1 Basic Science.

cases.name: Several learners, still one assignment
cases.title: Self study for three learners
cases.description: Give priya, amaka and chidi self study on fractions for JSS1 Mathematics.

expect.note: The tool takes a list. A model that calls it once per learner has spent three times the coins and made three assignments where the teacher asked for one.
